Face or Not?

Eigenfaces learned from 500 face windows rebuild other faces well and everything else badly. So the reconstruction error is a face detector's score: below a threshold, call the window a face. Here are 500 faces and 500 non-faces the eigenfaces never saw. Choose how many eigenfaces to use and where to put the threshold.

The face model

The decision

A window is called a face when its error is below the threshold. The slider is logarithmic, because the errors shrink a lot as k grows.

The score
pca_score normalizes a 31 × 25 window like the training faces, projects it onto the top k eigenfaces, rebuilds it, and returns the sum of squared differences between the window and its reconstruction. A face lies close to face space and rebuilds well; most other things do not.

    
AUC
The AUC is the probability that a randomly chosen face scores lower than a randomly chosen non-face (a tie counts half). 1.0 means some threshold separates them perfectly, 0.5 is a coin flip. It summarizes every threshold at once, so it changes with k but not with the threshold slider.

    
More is not better
With more eigenfaces the face space grows until it can rebuild nearly anything: the non-faces' errors fall along with the faces', and the gap between them closes. A good face model is good at faces and bad at everything else, which is why a few eigenfaces make a better detector than many.
